questionText: Your skin cancer detection AI (Artificial Intelligence) hits 98% accuracy on training data but drops to 65% on patients from different geographic regions. What is the most likely root cause?
options: Overfitting to Training Distribution
Data Shift (Representative Bias)
Suboptimal Learning Rate Schedule
Model Architecture Mismatch
explanation: Representative bias occurs when training data doesn't reflect the diversity of the real-world population where the model is deployed.
remediationNotes: Review Chapter 8 on Bias and Fairness in datasets.
learningObjective: Identify and explain data diversity failures.

questionText: A bank's complex model denies a loan. Regulators require a specific explanation for why the applicant was rejected. Which approach directly addresses this requirement?
options: Model Compression (Quantization)
XAI (Explainable AI (Artificial Intelligence)) Methods
A/B Testing with Control Groups
Transfer Learning from Pre-trained Models
explanation: Explainable AI (Artificial Intelligence) provides tools to make complex model decision-making interpretable and auditable by humans.
learningObjective: Apply explainability to a business scenario.

questionText: In a hospital, missing a serious diagnosis (False Negative) is far more dangerous than a false alarm (False Positive). Which metric should the AI (Artificial Intelligence) team prioritize?
options: Precision (Positive Predictive Value)
Recall (Sensitivity)
F1-Score (Harmonic Mean)
AUC-ROC (Area Under the Curve - Receiver Operating Characteristic) (Area Under the Curve - Receiver Operating Characteristic) (Overall Discrimination)
explanation: Recall measures the ability to find all positive cases. High recall ensures fewer diseases go undetected.
remediationNotes: Think: If you can't afford to MISS one, you need high Recall. See Ch 17.
learningObjective: Differentiate between precision and recall in a medical context.
option_d: AUC-ROC (Area Under the Curve - Receiver Operating Characteristic) (Area Under the Curve - Receiver Operating Characteristic) (Overall Discrimination)

questionText: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) retrieves documents before generating an answer. Why is this more reliable than relying solely on the LLM (Large Language Model)'s trained memory?
correctAnswer: It grounds answers in external facts, reducing hallucinations.
options: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) processes inputs faster than standard LLM (Large Language Model) inference.
It grounds answers in external facts, reducing hallucinations.
RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) retrains the model on new data overnight automatically.
RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) eliminates the need for any GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) processing.
explanation: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) provides context the model can reference before answering, preventing guessing based on outdated training data.
remediationNotes: Check the 'Grounding AI (Artificial Intelligence)' section in Chapter 16.
option_a: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) processes inputs faster than standard LLM (Large Language Model) inference.
option_b: It grounds answers in external facts, reducing hallucinations.
option_c: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) retrains the model on new data overnight automatically.
option_d: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) eliminates the need for any GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) processing.

questionText: A retailer wants a customized demand prediction model but has limited historical data. What is the core trade-off they face between building custom vs. using a pre-trained API (Application Programming Interface)?
correctAnswer: Custom models need more data and in-house expertise to build.
options: Pre-trained APIs (Application Programming Interfaces) require fine-tuning before any practical use.
Custom models need more data and in-house expertise to build.
Cloud APIs (Application Programming Interfaces) are never suitable for custom business use cases.
Model accuracy depends primarily on available hardware specifications.
explanation: Custom models offer better fit but require significant data and team effort compared to off-the-shelf AI (Artificial Intelligence) APIs (Application Programming Interfaces).
remediationNotes: Review Chapter 12 and 14 on Cloud AI (Artificial Intelligence) and build-vs-buy decisions.
learningObjective: Weigh the build-vs-buy decisions for AI (Artificial Intelligence).
option_a: Pre-trained APIs (Application Programming Interfaces) require fine-tuning before any practical use.
option_b: Custom models need more data and in-house expertise to build.
option_c: Cloud APIs (Application Programming Interfaces) are never suitable for custom business use cases.
option_d: Model accuracy depends primarily on available hardware specifications.

questionText: A fairness audit reveals your hiring AI (Artificial Intelligence) rejects more candidates from one demographic — yet no such rule exists in the code. What is the most likely cause?
correctAnswer: Proxy variables in training data correlate with protected attributes.
options: The training dataset is too small for generalization.
Proxy variables in training data correlate with protected attributes.
The model's interface is poorly designed for diverse users.
Training labels were stored in an incorrect file format.
explanation: Models can learn bias from proxies — data that isn't the sensitive attribute but is highly correlated with it (e.g., zip code correlating with race).
remediationNotes: Review Chapter 8 on 'Indirect Bias' and proxies.
learningObjective: Identify indirect bias in AI (Artificial Intelligence) systems.
option_a: The training dataset is too small for generalization.
option_b: Proxy variables in training data correlate with protected attributes.
option_c: The model's interface is poorly designed for diverse users.
option_d: Training labels were stored in an incorrect file format.

questionText: A developer wants to improve an LLM (Large Language Model)'s output on a niche legal summarization task without retraining the model. They consider Zero-Shot vs. Few-Shot prompting. What is the key difference?
correctAnswer: Zero-shot provides no examples; Few-shot includes example outputs in the prompt.
options: Zero-shot uses images; Few-shot uses only text input.
Zero-shot provides no examples; Few-shot includes example outputs in the prompt.
Zero-shot needs a GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) cluster; Few-shot runs on standard CPUs (Central Processing Units).
Both methods produce functionally identical results for all tasks.
explanation: Few-shot prompting is an in-context learning technique that significantly improves performance on narrow or complex tasks.
option_a: Zero-shot uses images; Few-shot uses only text input.
option_b: Zero-shot provides no examples; Few-shot includes example outputs in the prompt.
option_c: Zero-shot needs a GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) cluster; Few-shot runs on standard CPUs (Central Processing Units).
option_d: Both methods produce functionally identical results for all tasks.

questionText: A developer uses Vertex AI (Artificial Intelligence) to manage their entire model lifecycle. What is the primary advantage of this unified MLOps platform?
correctAnswer: It streamlines model training through reliable, monitored production deployment.
options: It generates full application front-end code automatically.
It streamlines model training through reliable, monitored production deployment.
It allows models to run without any power source.
It functions as a social network for AI (Artificial Intelligence) research teams.
explanation: MLOps focuses on deploying and maintaining ML (Machine Learning) models at scale reliably — Vertex AI (Artificial Intelligence) provides that unified pipeline.

questionText: In a classification model, a colleague suggests using overall accuracy as the sole success metric. Why is a Confusion Matrix a more informative evaluation tool?
correctAnswer: It shows predicted vs. true class breakdowns.
options: It calculates the total GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) cost of model training.
It shows predicted vs. true class breakdowns.
It syncs model weights to external cloud storage.
It randomizes training batches to reduce overfitting.
explanation: A confusion matrix exposes False Positives and False Negatives that overall accuracy hides, giving a complete picture of model behavior.
remediationNotes: Review the 'Performance Evaluation' section in Chapter 17.
learningObjective: Interpret a confusion matrix for classification tasks.
option_a: It calculates the total GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) cost of model training.
option_b: It shows predicted vs. true class breakdowns.
option_c: It syncs model weights to external cloud storage.
option_d: It randomizes training batches to reduce overfitting.

questionText: An AI (Artificial Intelligence) system is deployed at the edge of a remote factory rather than in a central cloud. What is the primary operational benefit of this architecture?
correctAnswer: Data stays local, reducing latency and protecting privacy.
options: The system has better resistance to physical shocks and vibration.
Data stays local, reducing latency and protecting privacy.
The AI (Artificial Intelligence) can autonomously repair malfunctioning hardware components.
The model consumes less electricity than cloud-based alternatives.
explanation: Edge computing processes data on-site, eliminating the lag of sending data to a central cloud and keeping sensitive data local.
remediationNotes: Review Chapter 16 tools for edge deployment.
